sentences.text: Task 1. Katie Chandra is the editor of the magazine.
She is holding a meeting with two journalists, Iris Moo and Dan Lai, about the next issue.
Listen to their discussion and complete the missing information in the spaces below.
One has been provided as an example.
You now have thirty seconds to study the task.
At the end of the task, you will have one minute to tidy up your answers.
Morning, Dan. You look very well.
Where's Katie? Hi Iris.
She's not here yet but she texted to say she’s on her way.
So um how was your weekend?
Oh, really terrible actually.
Oh dear. I’m sorry to hear that.
What was so awful about it?
Well, my dog was sick.
Oh no. Um, why was your dog sick?
I don’t know.
It was fine all week and then suddenly at the weekend it became really really sick.
Oh that’s terrible.
Well, I hope your dog gets better soon.
Thanks. How about you?
How was yours?
Well, I don’t mean to gloat, but I had a great weekend, a really wonderful weekend Do you want to know why?
Let me tell you.
I bought a new TV, one of those really really big TVs.
It’s totally amazing it’s like real life.
Wow! That sounds cool.
I would love to have a big TV like that.
Oh, here comes Katie now.
Morning guys. Sorry, I’m a bit late.
Morning Katie. So how was your weekend, Katie?
Ugh, Boring, boring, boring!
Why? Why? Why?
Because I had to work, work, work, Dan!
That's my reward for being the boss I suppose having to work all weekend!
Oh well. Right, now, we've got lots to get through.
So for the June edition of the magazine our main theme will be games and play.
Now, I sent out an email last week asking us all to come up with ideas for topics.
Dan? Well, I was thinking of computer games and learning, you know like games that actually teach you a skill.
There’s one called The Next Mozart It’s like a piano playing game.
My knees is always playing it Yeah, that is a good topic.
I'll definitely accept it for the next edition.
These computer games for learning are really popular.
Right, and what have you got for us, Iris?
Well, I’ve been looking at games that young children play in the playground.
Do you mean like playground games?
Yeah, that’s right, playground games.
I was thinking of looking at some examples, you know like Catch the Dragon and Fingers Out Oh yeah.
Did you say Fingers Out I remember Fingers Out I used to play that all the time when I was at primary school.
What was the first game called again?
The Dragon one, Catch the Dragon Oh right.
Not sure if I ever played that one.
Oh I did.
Definitely. Anyway, this is a great topic, Iris.
So you accept it?
Yep, definitely. Playground games are fun to watch.
Lots and lots of fun to watch So right back to you, Dan.
Any other contributions?
Yes. So something I've been looking at is computer games for animals.
I think it would be nice to contrast human games with, like, games animals play.
Well, it sounds interesting.
What do you mean by computer games for animals exactly?
Well, there’s loads of videos on the Internet.
Darks and cats jumping at moving objects on the computer screen.
It’s really funny.
There’s this one game you can get for computer tablets called Crazy Cats.
It’s brilliant. The cat chases a red dot around the screen.
Dan, you're not getting paid to look at funny videos on the Internet.
What research have you done?
Really. Crazy Cat Um, no research.
Sorry. Will you accept my topic though?
Dan you haven't done any research so it’s a no.
I can’t accept topics that haven’t been researched.
Yeah, OK.
